title: Liber De Scriptoribus Ecclesiasticis
author: Gennadius Massiliensis

passages.original: m JOANNES, Hierosolymorum episcopus, scripsit adversus obirectatores studii sui librum a, in quo ostendit Origenis sc ingenium, non fidem seculum.
passages.english: John, bishop of Jerusalem, wrote a book against the detractors of his own studies, in which he shows that he followed Origen's talent, not his faith.
passages.notes: Stray letters (m, a, sc) are taken as footnote marks. 'obirectatores' read as 'obtrectatores', 'seculum' as 'secutum'.

passages.original: I B THEOPHILUS, Alexandrinæ civitatis episcopus, h scripsit adversum Origenem unum ct grande volumen, quo omnia pene ejus dicta i et ipsum pa i er damnat, simul docens, non a se primum eum, sed ab antiquis Patribus, et maxime Heracla, fuisse et a presbyterio ejectum, et de ecclesia pulsum, i ct de civitate fugatum.
passages.english: Theophilus, bishop of the city of Alexandria, wrote one large volume against Origen, in which he condemns almost all of his sayings, and the man himself as well. He shows at the same time that Origen was not first [condemned] by him, but by the ancient Fathers, and especially Heraclas, and was expelled from the presbytery, driven out of the church, and put to flight from the city.
passages.notes: 'pa i er' read as 'pariter'; 'ct' as 'et'. Stray letters (I B, h, i) are omitted as marks. 'Heracla' is taken as Heraclas, bishop of Alexandria.

passages.original: II EuSEBIUS scripsit de crucis Domini Mysterio et apostolorum, præcipueque n Petri constantia, p virtute crucis indepta. ,
passages.english: Eusebius wrote on the mystery of the Lord's cross, and on the constancy of the apostles, and especially of Peter, which was obtained through the power of the cross.
passages.notes: This Eusebius is not otherwise identified in the passage. 'indepta' is taken as 'obtained'.

passages.original: b PELAGIUS hæresiarcha, antequam proderetur hæreticus, scripsit studiosis viris c, necessarios tres de Fide Trinitatis libros : et pro actuali conversatione d Eulogiarum ex Divinis Scripturos librum. unum , capitulorum indiciis, e in modum S. Cyprani martyris præsignatum.
passages.english: Pelagius the heresiarch, before he was exposed as a heretic, wrote three books On Faith in the Trinity, useful to studious men; and, for practical conduct of life, one book of Eulogiae (Extracts) from the Divine Scriptures, marked out in advance with chapter headings after the manner of the holy martyr Cyprian.
passages.notes: Footnote letters (b, c, d, e) omitted. 'Scripturos' read as 'Scripturis', 'Cyprani' as 'Cypriani'. 'Eulogiarum' is the title of a collection of scriptural extracts (testimonia), here likened to Cyprian's Testimonia.

passages.original: m JULIANUS, episcopus n Capuanus, vir acris insenii, in divinis Scripturis doctus, Græca ct Latina lingua scholasticus priusquam impietatem Pclagii in se aperiret, clarus in doctoribus Ecclesiæ fuit. Postea vero o hærcsim Pelagii defendere nisus, scripsit adversus Augustinum impugnatorem illius libros quatuor et iterum libros septem. Est etiam liber P altercationis amborum patres suas defendentium. lic Julianus eleemosynis tempore famis et angustiae indigentibus omnibus suis erogatis, multos miserationis specic I nobilium præcipue et religiosorum, illicicns hæresi suæ sociavit.
passages.english: Julian, bishop of Capua, a man of keen intellect, learned in the divine Scriptures, a scholar in the Greek and Latin languages, was distinguished among the teachers of the Church before he revealed in himself the impiety of Pelagius. But afterwards, having striven to defend the heresy of Pelagius, he wrote against Augustine, its opponent, four books, and again seven books. There is also a book of the dispute between the two, each defending his own side. This Julian, having given away all his possessions in alms to the needy in a time of famine and hardship, enticed many under the appearance of compassion, especially among the nobles and the religious, and joined them to his heresy.
passages.notes: Footnote letters (m, n, o, P, I) omitted; scanning errors corrected (insenii = ingenii, ct = et, Pclagii, hærcsim, lic = Hic, specic = specie, illicicns = illiciens). 'Capuanus' is the edition's reading; Julian is usually known as bishop of Eclanum, so this may be an error in the source or text. 'patres suas' is evidently corrupt, probably for 'partes suas' ('their own sides'), translated so.

passages.original: % m LEPORIUS adhuc monachus, pos ca presbyter, præsumens de puritate vitæ,quam arbitrio tantum et conatu proprio, non Dei se adjutorio ohtinuissc crediderat, Pelagianum a degma cœperat sequi. Scil a Gallicanis doctoribus admonitus, et in Africa per Augustinum a Dco emendatus, scripsit Emendationis suæ Libellum : in quo et satisfacit de errore, ct gratias agit de emendatione. Simul et quod male senserat, de incarnatione Christi corrigens b « catholicin sententiam tulit, dicens manentibus in Christo duabus naturis, c unam credi Filii Dei personam.
passages.english: Leporius, while still a monk and afterwards a presbyter, presuming on the purity of his life, which he believed he had obtained by his own will and effort alone and not by God's help, had begun to follow the Pelagian doctrine. But, admonished by Gallic teachers and corrected by God in Africa through Augustine, he wrote a Booklet of his Correction, in which he both makes amends for his error and gives thanks for his correction. At the same time, correcting also what he had wrongly held concerning the incarnation of Christ, he put forward the catholic view, saying that, while two natures remain in Christ, one person of the Son of God is to be believed in.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'pos ca' read as 'postea', 'degma' as 'dogma', 'Scil' as 'Sed', 'catholicin' as 'catholicam'. Stray marks are omitted.

passages.original: ad meam tamen notitiam ista sunt, quae venerunt: de Incarnatione Domini b adversus Eutychen presbyterum etc Dioscorum Alexandriae episcopum, qui humanam in Christo d carnem fuisse negant, scripta fortia, per quae confirmat et ratione et c testimoniis Scripturarum , ita illum veram maternae substantiae carnem habuisse, quam ex matre Virgine sumpsit, sicut et veram deitatem, quam f aeterna nascibilitate a Deo Patre gignente ipse nascendo accepit. Sunt et ejus decem Historiae ecclesiasticae libri g quos imitatus Eusebium Cæsariensem scripsit, incipiens a fine librorum Eusebii usque ad suum tempus , id est, a Vicennalibus Constantini usque ad imperium Leonis senioris, sub quo et mortuus est.
passages.english: Yet these are the [works] that have come to my notice: forceful writings on the Incarnation of the Lord against the presbyter Eutyches and Dioscorus, bishop of Alexandria, who deny that there was human flesh in Christ. In these he confirms, both by reason and by testimonies of the Scriptures, that He had true flesh of His mother's substance, which He took from the Virgin mother, just as He had true deity, which by being born He received through eternal birth from God the Father who begot [Him]. There are also his ten books of Ecclesiastical History, which he wrote in imitation of Eusebius of Caesarea. He begins from the end of Eusebius' books and continues to his own time, that is, from the Vicennalia of Constantine to the reign of Leo the Elder, under whom he also died.
passages.notes: The subject is Theodoret, bishop of Cyrrhus, named in the preceding context. 'etc' is read as 'et'. 'Ten books' does not match the five books of Theodoret's surviving history; the author may be confusing him with another historian. 'nascibilitate' is an unusual word, rendered here as 'birth'. The Vicennalia were the celebrations of Constantine's twentieth year of rule.
